feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid public-sector specialization. It is well written overall, but it feels slightly dense and repetitive, and a few style/consistency issues reduce polish.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, culminating in leadership roles with increasing scope, budget, governance, analytics, and platform ownership.  
- Good use of scale indicators and concrete detail: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” and named tools/platforms add credibility.  
- Strong positioning for modern digital leadership through a blend of strategy, CMS/web delivery, analytics, multimedia, and AI-enabled search.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition across summary, competencies, skills, and project descriptions; “digital strategy / governance / workflows / AI-enabled” appears many times. Consolidating would improve clarity and impact.  
- Tighten structure and formatting: the footer “Recent Projects” reads like a compressed paragraph, and some bullets are overly long. Consider moving projects into a dedicated section with 2–3 concise bullets each.  
- Fix stylistic inconsistencies and minor grammar/punctuation issues: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; “organization-wide” vs. “organization wide” should be standardized; “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual unless intentional branding. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience sections. Tightening it and adding one concrete scale cue would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” with more direct, active phrasing.
- Add a concrete scale marker from recent experience, e.g., “10,000+ page websites,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ publishers.”
- Streamline the service list to 3–4 priority areas most relevant to target roles: web modernization, governance/editorial systems, analytics, and AI-enabled search/UX.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing high-volume public-sector web ecosystems. Leads enterprise website transformation, digital governance, analytics infrastructure, and editorial operations for complex, mission-driven organizations, including 10,000+ page platforms serving millions of annual users.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; consider narrowing to “AI-enabled search.”
- “Multimedia production” is already well covered in experience and skills; it may not need prominence in the intro.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the headline and recent roles, but this section currently overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-level leadership capabilities would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and sharpen wording: “Enterprise web modernization,” “Editorial governance and publishing systems,” “Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure.”
- Replace broader or vaguer items with more distinctive strengths: “AI-enabled search and content discovery” is clearer than “content experiences.”
- Consider a more executive-focused version: Enterprise web modernization • Editorial governance and publishing systems • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Cross-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Keep “cross-channel” or “multi-channel” consistent with usage elsewhere in the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; keep it shorter and more strategic rather than restating tools or detailed functions.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with multiple experience bullets; retain only if targeting communications leadership roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense for a footer. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing to reinforce recency and distinguish this from core experience.
- Use parallel, tighter phrasing: start each item with a strong verb and reduce stacked nouns (e.g., “hybrid retrieval, vector search, and AI chat”).
- Add one concrete outcome, audience, or scale detail where possible for 1–2 projects.
- Standardize style and punctuation; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for consistency and readability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, anniversary campaign, and advocacy video series all overlap with Work Experience; keep this section shorter and more portfolio-like rather than restating responsibilities.
- “Built” repeats across multiple items; vary verbs such as “Designed,” “Launched,” “Produced,” or “Developed.”

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consulting impact, platform modernization, and the AI/search work.

Suggested edit
- Open with outcome + scope: “Advise the National Association of Counties on digital strategy, enterprise web modernization, and communications operations for member-facing platforms.”
- Collapse overlapping duties into 3–4 sharper bullets focused on consulting value: digital systems/workflows/analytics; Drupal campaign builds; governance across channels; AI-enabled search initiative.
- Replace generic verbs (“consult,” “build and refine,” “deliver”) with stronger phrasing: “Architected,” “Led,” “Designed,” “Standardized,” “Improved.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, toolkit downloads, publishing time reduced, search relevance gains, stakeholder teams served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Drupal microsites/toolkits” and “AI-enabled search” duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and let projects hold the detail.
- “Governance, analytics, workflows” also echoes the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize post-director consulting scope and advisory leadership.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Prioritize the most distinctive wins first: website modernization, analytics infrastructure, and in-house studio build.
- Make channel oversight more outcome-based: replace “reaching tens of thousands” / “serving thousands” with performance, growth, engagement, or campaign impact if available.
- Possible rewrite:
- Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget.
- Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring multimedia series.
- Implemented analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery; improved reporting, governance, and cross-department planning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Newsletter/social management overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role.
- “Governance/publishing workflows” also appears in the current consulting role; keep wording distinct.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Tighten it around operational leadership, newsletter ownership, and the launch/expansion of repeatable advocacy video.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy publishing.”
- Make bullets more outcome-focused: “Owned production of four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Strengthen the video bullet: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring channel for policy communications.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper operations point: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Helping scale” and “helped improve” are weak and repetitive; use direct action verbs.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered more strategically in the Director of Digital Media entry.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and framed around senior-level scope rather than broad communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less redundant phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing systems & workflow design
- Cross-channel communications operations leadership
- Public-sector advocacy campaigns & stakeholder messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy & information architecture
- Consider swapping “audience-focused content planning” for “information architecture” or “content operations” to better reflect recent, higher-level work.
- Keep terms aligned with recent experience: governance, modernization, workflows, cross-channel operations, AI/search-adjacent strategy.
- If space is tight, cut “public-sector” here since it is already clear elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with multiple NACo experience bullets; make this skills item more systems/governance-focused.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. For a topline skills item, emphasize higher-value capabilities tied to recent Drupal modernization, integrations, automation, and AI search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put the most relevant/recent strengths first: Drupal, CMS modernization, API/workflow integration, AI-enabled search.
- Consider dropping lower-priority platforms unless job-relevant; “WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages” can be grouped as “additional CMS platforms.”
- If space allows, add scope language: “enterprise CMS modernization” or “public-sector web platforms” to reinforce seniority and context.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search experiences” duplicates Core Competencies and recent project content; keep here only if shortened elsewhere.
- Most tools repeat the Technical + IT section; this topline item should stay strategic, not exhaustive.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for the recent Director/Consultant work, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something more outcome-led, e.g. “Analytics Infrastructure, Reporting & Optimization.”
- Replace the flat list with grouped, sharper phrasing: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, BigQuery, Looker Studio and Power BI” + “KPI framework design, executive reporting and performance analysis.”
- Add one strategic capability instead of another tool, such as “measurement strategy” or “insight-driven optimization,” to show leadership beyond platform familiarity.
- If space allows, tighten to: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI • KPI and measurement framework design • Executive reporting • SEO and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and the “Data, Analytics & Optimization” Technical + IT section.
- Consider keeping tools in Technical + IT and using this topline item to emphasize strategic analytics leadership.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level production leadership and event delivery rather than basic task skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools/tasks to scope and level: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems • Virtual event execution”
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” to better match the studio-building achievement in the 2022–2024 role.
- Replace “Livestreaming” with “Livestream and hybrid event delivery” for stronger phrasing and clearer event context.
- If space allows, use “Multi-camera/PTZ systems” instead of just “PTZ camera systems” to sound more outcome-oriented and less equipment-list-like.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating that exact phrase here.
- Detailed tools are already covered under “Multimedia & Creative Tools,” so keep this section strategic, not software-focused.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add level/context or be tightened to emphasize the most current, highest-value platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strategic relevance and recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine if Drupal-led work is the focus; consider adding qualifiers.
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector web modernization) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add proficiency framing rather than just names: **Enterprise CMS: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages; lightweight publishing: GitHub Pages**
- Consider dropping **GitHub Pages** if it was only lightly used; it reads less central than the rest.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep one version broader and this one more tool-specific.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so don’t repeat that phrase here unless you remove it from Topline Skills.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. For a senior digital leader, this section should emphasize implementation scope and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for specificity and seniority: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group by function to improve scanability: “Integrations & deployment: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Workers”
- If accurate, add outcome/context signals instead of only tools, e.g. “used for CMS customization, campaign microsites, tagging, automation, and edge-based web enhancements”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with Topline Skills: “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations”; avoid repeating identical phrasing
- GTM also overlaps conceptually with analytics infrastructure elsewhere; keep this item focused on implementation, not reporting

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since the CV already emphasizes automation and governance, this item should be tighter and grouped to signal systems thinking, not just familiarity.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function to improve scan value: “Automation & workflow systems: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; Work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Put the strongest/most relevant tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier should lead because they align with recent workflow/operations work.
- Consider dropping 1–2 lower-value/general collaboration tools if space is tight; Slack and Teams are widely assumed unless used for structured workflow orchestration.
- If accurate, add a qualifier such as “workflow design, intake systems, approvals, and cross-team coordination” to connect tools to outcomes.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp overlap as project-management tools; listing all four may feel redundant unless each was materially used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of email/engagement capability. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and platform-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform names for readability and consistency: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope instead of more tools: **Enterprise email automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; if one was limited or older, remove it rather than padding the list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with recent work experience describing newsletter/email leadership; avoid repeating outcomes here.
- “Multi-channel communications” and email operations already appear in Core Competencies, so don’t expand this into a responsibility statement.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and repeats analytics platforms already proven in the recent Director role. Tighten it to emphasize optimization capabilities, not just software names.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Testing & Optimization**
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI reporting • dashboard development • SEO analysis • A/B testing**
- Put the most strategic/recently evidenced tools first: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity.
- Replace generic “Dashboarding” with stronger phrasing like **dashboard development** or **executive reporting**; if accurate, add a measurable qualifier elsewhere in experience (e.g., reporting for 3.5M annual page views or 50+ publishers).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping detail in one place and shortening the other.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating identical wording across sections.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and anchor it in “firsts,” team-building, and concrete outputs.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-stage build work: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Tighten the second sentence around visible contributions: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, for member and advocacy communications.”
- Clarify supervision without overstating: “Provided day-to-day direction and production support for a digital media associate.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social output, or efficiency gains from workflow improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this version framed as launching/producing the format, while the later role shows scaling it.
- Avoid repeating broad “web, email, social, video” channel coverage already stated more strongly in later positions.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize the podcast launch and any concrete program/research outputs rather than broad coordination language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and policy research initiatives for NACo programs; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer scope: “Produced digital and multimedia materials supporting member programs and policy communications.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes launched, research projects supported, stakeholders served, or audience/download growth.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles so progression is clear.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager / Producer and Associate Communications Director entries.
- Avoid repeating video/livestream language here unless this role truly owned it; podcast launch is the unique differentiator.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities. It also overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” elsewhere, so it should be tightened to emphasize tools only or framed more strategically.
